# EventRegistry { #timetoalign.EventRegistry }

```python
EventRegistry(timeline_id, data, *, host=None)
```

The registry rows of the events of one or more families, as a view.

A view is a filter over the families it reads, read when asked: it
follows the rows as they change. :attr:`table` holds one row per event
in the columns of :data:`REGISTRY_SCHEMA`, positions on each family's
root axis; :meth:`content` the content of the events of one kind. The
rows recording where a child lies (:data:`SEGMENT_KIND`) are no events
and no view shows them.

Rows come in through the doors of package readers and loaders, on a
view too: :meth:`add_rows` (rows read from a package), :meth:`update`
(a parser's new run, :meth:`update_target` the timeline it updates);
writers read through :meth:`written`. A timeline adds its own rows
through :meth:`Timeline.add_events
<timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.add_events>`.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type                                                                | Description                                                                                                                                                          | Default    |
|-------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| timeline_id | [str](`str`)                                                        | The ID of the root timeline of a new family.                                                                                                                         | _required_ |
| data        | [EventData](`timetoalign.storage.events.EventData`)                 | The root's events, on its axis; their class is the class of the family's events. The parses it carries (:attr:`EventData.parses`) are held with them.                | _required_ |
| host        | [RegistryHost](`timetoalign.storage.registry.RegistryHost`) \| None | The timeline holding its events here (:class:`RegistryHost`): rows read for it are held within its length and its Boxes checked. None for a registry standing alone. | `None`     |

## Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                             |
|--------|----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If *data* holds one event ID twice, or names a parse it does not carry. |

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> from fractions import Fraction
>>> from timetoalign.timelines import ContinuousLogicalTimeline
>>> root = ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=8, unit="quarters", uid="clt_root")
>>> child = ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=4, unit="quarters", uid="clt_a")
>>> child.add_events([{"id": "a1", "event_type": "Beat", "start": Fraction(1, 2)}])
['a1']
>>> root.add_child(child, offset=2)
>>> root.registry.filter(kinds="Beat").table.column("start")[0].as_py()["value"]
2.5
>>> child.events.table.column("start")[0].as_py()["value"]
0.5
```

### add { #timetoalign.EventRegistry.add }

```python
EventRegistry.add(timeline_id, data, *, parse=None)
```

Add *data*'s rows to the timeline *timeline_id*, after its rows.

*data* is on the timeline's axis, in its own coordinates; the
registry rows are shifted onto the root's, column-wise. The columns
``locator`` and ``parse_id``, where *data* holds them, are moved
into the registry rows. A row naming no parse names
*parse*, else the family's tool parse
(:meth:`Parse.of_tool`, one per family). The parses *data*
carries (:attr:`EventData.parses`) that the rows name are held
with them. Taken by the registry of one family (a timeline's
``_registry``), not by a view.

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|--------|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [KeyError](`KeyError`)     | If the family holds no timeline *timeline_id*.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|        | [TypeError](`TypeError`)   | If this registry is a view.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If *data* lies on another axis than the family's, an event ID of it is held in the family or twice in *data*, a row names a parse neither held, nor *parse*, nor carried by *data*, a locator names two events of one parse, or a column of it holds values of a type the timeline's column does not read; nothing changes then. |

### add_rows { #timetoalign.EventRegistry.add_rows }

```python
EventRegistry.add_rows(rows, contents=None, parses=(), *, registered=True)
```

Hold registry rows already on the root's axis, as read from a package.

Each row joins the family of the timeline it names, among the
families this registry (a view too: a timeline's, a group's, a
bundle's) reads. A row the family holds already, on the same
timeline, of the same kind, at the same root position (``start`` and
``duration`` compared cell for cell), is passed over: it is the
event a manifest states inline. Each timeline taking rows is held
long enough for them, as for the rows it adds itself (an unlocked
timeline grows to the last end, made local by its ancestors'
offsets; a locked one refuses). The rows' content is read lazily:
the family's events are built from its rows and *contents* (per
kind, a table keyed by ``id`` or a callable giving one) when a
timeline's events are first read, positions made local (the root
position less the offsets of the timeline's ancestors), each
timeline's in the order of its rows; a timeline taking a Box reads
its events at once and checks every Box against its shape, as a Box
added is checked.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name       | Type                                                                                                                                                                                               | Description                                                                                                              | Default    |
|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| rows       | [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`)                                                                                                                                                           | Registry rows (:data:`REGISTRY_SCHEMA`'s columns; a column absent is null), ``start`` and ``duration`` as storage cells. | _required_ |
| contents   | [Mapping](`collections.abc.Mapping`)\[[str](`str`), [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`) \| [Callable](`collections.abc.Callable`)\[\[\], [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`)\]\] \| None | The content of each kind, keyed by ``id``; every family taking rows reads it (each its own events' rows).                | `None`     |
| parses     | [Iterable](`collections.abc.Iterable`)\[[Parse](`timetoalign.storage.registry.Parse`)\]                                                                                                            | The parses the rows name; each family taking rows holds them all.                                                        | `()`       |
| registered | [bool](`bool`)                                                                                                                                                                                     | The rows are a package's: a family taking them never joins a parent afterwards.                                          | `True`     |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|--------|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [KeyError](`KeyError`)     | If a row names a timeline no family of this registry holds.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If a row lies on another axis than its family's, names a parse not given or held, holds an ID held in the family or twice, a locator naming two events of one parse, ends past the length of a locked timeline, or a Box contradicts its shape. Nothing changes then, but the lengths of timelines grown before a refusal. |

### concat { #timetoalign.EventRegistry.concat }

```python
EventRegistry.concat(*registries)
```

One view of the rows of *registries*, each row once.

A family read by several of them keeps the rows any of them keeps,
in the family's order; families in the order they first appear.

### content { #timetoalign.EventRegistry.content }

```python
EventRegistry.content(kind, ids=None)
```

The content of this view's events of *kind*, keyed by ``id``.

The columns of the events' own (a pre-parsed table's): ``id`` first,
then every column an event of *kind* holds a value in (its name
among them), without its position, type or registry columns. One row per event of
*kind* this view holds (of *ids* only, if given), in the view's
order.

### counts { #timetoalign.EventRegistry.counts }

```python
EventRegistry.counts(by='kind')
```

The number of rows per value of the column *by*, sorted by value.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

|        | [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`) | (null last); the total is ``len(registry)``.                  |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                   | Description                    |
|--------|------------------------|--------------------------------|
|        | [KeyError](`KeyError`) | If *by* is no registry column. |

### filter { #timetoalign.EventRegistry.filter }

```python
EventRegistry.filter(
    within=None,
    kinds=None,
    parses=None,
    vanished=None,
    min_coord=None,
    max_coord=None,
)
```

A view of the rows of this one meeting every condition given.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name      | Type                                                                           | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Default   |
|-----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| within    | [str](`str`) \| [Iterable](`collections.abc.Iterable`)\[[str](`str`)\] \| None | Keep the rows of these timelines (IDs).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `None`    |
| kinds     | [str](`str`) \| [Iterable](`collections.abc.Iterable`)\[[str](`str`)\] \| None | Keep the rows of these kinds (event types).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | `None`    |
| parses    | [str](`str`) \| [Iterable](`collections.abc.Iterable`)\[[str](`str`)\] \| None | Keep the rows made by these parses (IDs).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | `None`    |
| vanished  | [bool](`bool`) \| None                                                         | True keeps the rows an update no longer found, False the others; None keeps both.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `None`    |
| min_coord | [Any](`typing.Any`)                                                            | Keep the rows starting at or after this position (inclusive), compared as :meth:`EventData.filter` compares a bound: exactly where it is exact and the axis ``int`` or ``fraction``, as a key where it is a float. A bare number lies on each family's root axis; a ``Coordinate`` keeps rows of the families in its unit only (no row of a family on another unit lies at it); an ``IdCoordinate`` lies on the timeline it names, moved onto that timeline's root by the offsets of its ancestors, and keeps rows of that family only. | `None`    |
| max_coord | [Any](`typing.Any`)                                                            | Keep the rows starting before this position (exclusive), read as *min_coord*.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | `None`    |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                |
|--------|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If a bound is NaN, when the rows are read. |

### update { #timetoalign.EventRegistry.update }

```python
EventRegistry.update(data, parse, *, timeline_id=None)
```

Update the rows of a timeline of this registry from *data*, a parser's new run.

*data* holds the rows of one parse, local to the timeline they
were read for, each with its ``locator`` (a column). The timeline
updated is :meth:`update_target`'s. Its rows are matched by the full
``locator`` among the rows made by parses of the same source as
*parse*: a matched row keeps its ID and takes the new row's
content, position and *parse*; a new row matching none is
added; an old row of that source no longer found is kept, naming
*parse* in ``vanished_in``. Nothing is deleted. A view (a
timeline's, a group's, a bundle's) updates the family holding the
timeline.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type                                                | Description                                    | Default    |
|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------|------------|
| data        | [EventData](`timetoalign.storage.events.EventData`) | The rows read again, with their locators.      | _required_ |
| parse       | [Parse](`timetoalign.storage.registry.Parse`)       | The run that read them.                        | _required_ |
| timeline_id | [str](`str`) \| None                                | The timeline updated where no locator matches. | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type         | Description                     |
|--------|--------------|---------------------------------|
|        | [str](`str`) | The ID of the timeline updated. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                                                                                                                             |
|--------|----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If *data* gives no locators or one locator twice, matches no timeline of this registry (by locator or by ID), lies on another axis, or an added row's ID is held; nothing changes then. |

### update_target { #timetoalign.EventRegistry.update_target }

```python
EventRegistry.update_target(data, parse, *, timeline_id=None)
```

The timeline :meth:`update` would update from *data*, or None.

The timeline of this registry holding most of the rows that *data*'s
locators name among the rows made by parses of the same source
file as *parse* (ties: the timeline met first); where they name
none, the timeline *timeline_id* (else the one *data* is a table of)
if a family of this registry holds it. Read column-wise: one table
of each held parse's ID and source, and set lookups.

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                         |
|--------|----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If *data* gives no locators (a column ``locator``). |

### written { #timetoalign.EventRegistry.written }

```python
EventRegistry.written(kinds=None)
```

What a writer stores of the events of the families this view reads.

Every family this view reads, whole (a package holds a family whole:
a child's events lie on its root's axis), its rows and contents read
when asked. The rows recording where a child lies (a ``Segment`` row
named by a timeline of the family) are left out; a user's
``Segment`` row, an event like any other, is kept, naming the
family's parse of events made in code
(:meth:`Parse.of_tool`) where it names none.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                                                                           | Description                                                           | Default   |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| kinds  | [str](`str`) \| [Iterable](`collections.abc.Iterable`)\[[str](`str`)\] \| None | Keep the rows and contents of these kinds only; every kind when None. | `None`    |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                          | Description                                              |
|--------|---------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [WrittenEvents](`timetoalign.storage.registry.WrittenEvents`) | The rows, the contents per timeline and kind, the parses |
|        | [WrittenEvents](`timetoalign.storage.registry.WrittenEvents`) | the rows name and the families                           |
|        | [WrittenEvents](`timetoalign.storage.registry.WrittenEvents`) | (:class:`WrittenEvents`).                                |
